---
title: "phibble for Laravel developers"
---

Analyze Eloquent query results with phibble, either collected into a
`DataFrame` or summarized in the database. `composer require phpstats/phibble`
is the whole setup, since package discovery registers two macros:

- `->toDataFrame()` on collections and query builders returns an in-memory
  `DataFrame`.
- `->phibble()` on query builders, Eloquent builders, and relations returns a
  lazy `SqlTable` that compiles table methods to SQL.

## Example data {#the-example-data}

Each example on this page queries this model, over a `penguins` table loaded
from the Palmer penguins data in the
[PHPstats datasets](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#penguins):

```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

final class Penguin extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'penguins';

    public $timestamps = false;

    public function scopeMeasured($query)
    {
        return $query->whereNotNull('body_mass_g');
    }
}
```

## DataFrames from collections and queries {#from-a-collection-or-query-to-a-dataframe}

{{< include examples/_laravel-to-dataframe.md >}}

- Column types are inferred from the values, as in `DataFrame::fromRows()`.
- Eloquent casts and accessors apply only to loaded models, as after `get()`
  here. `Penguin::query()->toDataFrame()` reads the raw rows.

## Lazy queries {#queries-that-stay-in-the-database}

{{< include examples/_laravel-phibble.md >}}

- The builder's SQL, bindings, and scopes become the table's source, and
  phibble's methods add to that query.
- Nothing runs until the rows are needed, as with `collect()`, printing, or
  `nrow()`.
- Global scopes such as `SoftDeletes` apply. Attribute casts and accessors do
  not, because the rows come from SQL.

This grouped filter keeps the heaviest penguin on each island.

- The comparison with the group maximum compiles to a window function.
- A PHP closure, or an expression that SQL cannot evaluate as R does, makes
  the table collect its rows and continue in memory as a `DataFrame`.

## phplyr {#with-phplyr}

[phplyr](https://github.com/phpstats/phplyr) runs dplyr's functions on the same
lazy table, so this pipeline also runs in the database.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}
## PHP 8.5+

```php
use function Phplyr\{
    arrange, col, desc, filter, group_by, mean, n, summarize,
};

$summary = Penguin::query()->phibble() |>
    filter(col('year')->ge(2008)) |>
    group_by('species', 'sex') |>
    summarize(
        n: n(),
        mass: mean(col('body_mass_g'), naRm: true),
    ) |>
    arrange(desc('mass'));
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```php
use function Phplyr\{col, desc, mean, n, phplyr};

$summary = phplyr(Penguin::query()->phibble())
    ->filter(col('year')->ge(2008))
    ->groupBy('species', 'sex')
    ->summarize(
        n: n(),
        mass: mean(col('body_mass_g'), naRm: true),
    )
    ->arrange(desc('mass'))
    ->get();
```
:::

- phplyr's `col()` and aggregates take camelCase options, as in `naRm`.

## Charts with phiz

[phiz](https://phiz.phpstats.org/docs) builds Vega-Lite charts in the style
of ggplot2, and `Plot::of()` accepts a `DataFrame`.

{{< include examples/_laravel-chart.md >}}

For a summary, group and aggregate in the database, so only the summary rows
reach PHP:

{{< include examples/_laravel-chart-summary.md >}}

In a Blade view, phiz's component renders a plot, and `@phizScripts` loads
the Vega libraries once per page:

```blade
<x-phiz :plot="$plot" />

@phizScripts
```

## Results {#using-the-result}

- `$df->toRows()` gives a list of associative arrays, for JSON responses and
  Blade loops.
- `$df->toJson()` gives the rows as a JSON string, and `toJson('columns')`
  gives the columns.
- `$df->toCollection()` returns a Laravel collection of rows.
- `$df->toModelData()` gives the columns in the form phit's model functions
  accept.

## Example setup {#running-the-examples}

The example scripts run outside a Laravel application.
[`support/laravel.php`](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble/blob/main/docs/examples/support/laravel.php)
creates an in-memory SQLite connection, loads the CSV, registers the macros,
and defines `Penguin`.
